messages:
Maria P: seeing a p99 CPU spike on telemetry-exporter when retention trimming is enabled, correlates with a big span volume surge during the nightly rollout. anyone else seeing this?
Sanjay K: yup. p99 jumped from ~200ms to ~4s on exporter process around 02:11. flamegraph points at encoding/json.Marshal and our retention.TrimSpan.
Kei L: which exporter? s3-archiver or the streaming kafka one?
Maria P: s3-archiver. quick snippet from pprof (top):
```
(pprof) top10
flat  cum   name
1.8s  3.4s  encoding/json.Marshal
1.2s  1.2s  bytes.(*Buffer).Write
0.9s  0.9s  telemetry/retention.TrimSpan
0.6s  0.6s  runtime.mallocgc
```
Sanjay K: reproduces locally if I replay logs that create many high-card spans with big attribute maps. allocation profiles show large map copies.
Anya V: iirc TrimSpan copies the attributes map then deletes keys to keep only allowed ones. that double-allocates. we should avoid deep-copying on the hot path. ideas: in-place mutate + annotate, or move trimming to background before encoding.
Kei L: streaming encoder would help too. if we can avoid building a full intermediate JSON blob per span and instead stream spans into the gzip/s3 writer, allocs drop. also protobuf path is much lighter in our benches.
Sanjay K: quick bench results: json path (current) avg allocs 2.4MB/batch, proto path ~0.9MB/batch. batch size = 128 spans for the test.
Maria P: interesting — batch size seems important. at batch=16 CPU p99 stays ~300ms but throughput drops. at 128 we hit the spike.
Kei L: we should try these experiments: toggle proto encoding behind feature flag, add sync.Pool for buffers and attribute maps, and try streaming JSON encoder + smaller default batch size.
InfraBot: deploy telemetry-exporter v2026.3 started by @deploy-bot to staging at 2026-03-17T02:10:12Z :rocket:
Maria P: hold on the rollout to prod for now, there's a correlation with the spike.
Anya V: quick micro-optimization: instead of map copy we can iterate allowed keys and build a small buffer of key/values in-place. if most spans have < 8 relevant attrs this is cheap.
Sanjay K: ran a quick patch replacing map-copy with selective write -> allocs dropped ~40% on my dev replay. pushing benchmark PR with traces.
Kei L: also we should measure encoder CPU vs gzip CPU tradeoff. maybe current chokepoint is marshal + allocs, not compression.
Maria P: i started a profiling run with proto flag on and smaller batch (32) on staging, link: https://pprof.internal.redwood/19472/pprof.html  (will share logs).
InfraBot: deploy telemetry-exporter v2026.3 rolled back to v2026.2 in prod by @deploy-bot at 2026-03-17T02:14:58Z :warning:
Maria P: thanks for the rollback. next steps i propose: 1) enable proto path behind flag and run 24h A/B, 2) add sync.Pool for buffers + reuse maps where safe, 3) reduce default batch to 32 and add autoscale triggers, 4) follow-up on streaming encoder for json.
Kei L: i'll pick up the pool + batch change. Anya can you own the proto path toggle and compatibility tests? Sanjay can you finish the benchmark PR and add the allocation profile to the test harness?
Anya V: yep i'll start the proto PR and add backward-compat tests for the archived format.
Sanjay K: PR up in a few hours with bench results. will include a quick script to reproduce with synthetic span volume.
Kei L: thanks. ping me for review, aiming for small, incremental changes so we can re-enable retention trimming without the spike. :thumbsup:
